what: Reusable saved prompts that steer Gemini on a task, rolling out to Workspace and replacing Gems.
pitch: WPR's repeat jobs — house style, headline sets, meeting-agenda summaries — become one saved instruction two people can both reuse, instead of re-typing prompts. Gems are being phased out, so existing setups need moving.
access: free — included with the Gemini app and Workspace plans; Workspace rollout over coming weeks

name: Native Markdown files in Google Docs and Drive
what: Open, edit and comment on .md files directly in Docs, with formatted previews in Drive.
pitch: Chatbots hand back Markdown. Until now pasting it into Docs mangled tables and headings. From October 5 it opens clean, keeps comments, and two editors can work on it live.
access: free — all Workspace customers and personal Google accounts, rolling out from October 5

name: AI Engine 3.8.3 for WordPress
what: WordPress plugin adding an on-site chatbot, AI forms and a writing assistant in the editor.
pitch: The October 1 update fixes the Editor Assistant session errors that broke mid-edit, stops replies cutting off mid-sentence, and makes non-OpenAI chatbots actually read your uploaded knowledge — the parts a two-person newsroom touches.
access: free core plugin on WordPress.org; optional paid Pro add-on, and you supply your own AI account

name: Notion AI: rebuilt agents, new Auto router and credit system
what: Notion's AI agents get their own browser, 24-hour tasks, a review mode and cheaper model routing.
pitch: Notion's biggest AI update of the year, shipped Monday. For a two-person newsroom it turns the story tracker into something that actually does the chasing between editions.
access: paid — free plan has limited AI credits; new credit system across plans; can connect your own ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Go plan

name: Gmail AI Inbox for paid Workspace accounts
what: Gmail view that pulls action items and deadlines out of threads and summarizes topics.
pitch: Rolled out October 15 to business Workspace accounts, not just consumer Gmail. Tip emails, records-request replies and advertiser threads stop getting buried when two people share the inbox load.
access: paid — included with Business Starter/Standard/Plus and Enterprise plans; US English only for now

name: Inbox Zero email client (open source)
what: Free, open-source AI email app for Gmail and Outlook on web, desktop and iPhone.
pitch: A credible free alternative to Superhuman that hit Product Hunt's top ten last week. The client itself costs nothing, so WPR can test AI email triage without a subscription decision.
access: open-source (AGPL) client, free; AI assistant tiers from $18/user/month annual, $20 monthly

name: Routine next steps on the Google Meet post-meeting screen
what: One-tap routines that draft follow-up emails or push meeting action items into Google Tasks.
pitch: Announced October 12. Small but real: the two of you stop re-typing what Gemini already captured, and recurring board or source calls hand off their own to-dos.
access: paid — Workspace plans with Gemini; requires 'Take notes for me' on during the meeting

name: AI Engine 3.8.5 / 3.8.6 for WordPress
what: Security-fix releases for the popular WordPress AI plugin, plus a one-click Claude site connector.
pitch: Two patch releases on October 14 and 17 fix real permission leaks — one where site data tools could return API keys, another letting editors alter posts they shouldn't. Update the WPR site this week.
